newsitem.title: USA: Merrill still optimistic about chip recovery.
newsitem.headline: Merrill still optimistic about chip recovery.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlak said he continues to be "optimistic about the recovery now developing in the (semiconductor) industry, although it's mostly in the PC area still."

The influential analyst said orders are improving and with "strong demand for microprocessors and DRAMs, we're looking for the possibility of a panic buying situation for these devices in the short-term. Also, the semiconductor industry doesn't respond quickly to higher orders. It takes several months to raise output. Consequently, that will tighten the market and (lift) spot prices for chips in the next few months."
"That should serve to improve book to bill to one to 1.15 at end-year," Kurlak said.

He expects September book-to-bill, set for release after today's market close, to come in at 1.00 -- higher than the average forecast of 0.94 to 0.95. The book-to-bill ratio is tallied by the U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association and measures new orders against sales in a month.
Kurlak said when he addressed Merrill's sales force this morning, he specifically mentioned Intel Corp, Texas Instruments Inc and Micron Technology Inc.
He established a two-year price target of $160 for Intel.
He also set two-year price objectives of $85-90 for Texas Instruments and $55 on Micron.
Intel was trading 3/8 higher to 105 in the U.S. pre-open, matching its 12-month high. Micron ended Monday at 31-1/8 and Texas Instruments finished at 54-1/4.
"I set a two-year price target given their recent runup. I don't see a straight line up. There will be bumps in the night," the analyst said.
Kurlak stressed he had not become more bullish on the group but reviewed his position with Merrill's sales force and set the two-year price targets on the three companies.
